discovery: Discovery of intrinsic magnetism in atomically thin van der Waals crystals
subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D magnetism and quantum materials)
motivation: In 2017, Xu and Jarillo-Herrero (in CrI3) and Zhang (in Cr2Ge2Te6) showed that long-range magnetic order survives down to single atomic layers of van der Waals crystals. The Mermin-Wagner theorem forbids such order in the isotropic 2D limit, and these experiments showed how magnetic anisotropy gets around it. Their work created the field of 2D magnetism. They found layer-dependent ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic ground states, and later showed electrical and gate control of magnetism, giant tunneling magnetoresistance in spin-filter junctions, and magnetic proximity effects in heterostructures. Atomically thin magnets are now a platform for studying magnons, excitons coupled to spin order, 2D multiferroics, and magnetism controlled by stacking and twisting. The work has shaped spintronics and quantum materials research worldwide, and it has been independently reproduced in many laboratories.
